sentences.text: Haplocanthosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur whose name translates to "simple-spine lizard".
This name refers to the simple dorsal spines on its vertebrae, which were not double-spined like other sauropods from the same formation.
It was one of the smallest Morrison sauropods, reaching a length of 14.8 meters and a weight of 12.8 metric tons.
Other estimates suggest a total length of around 15 meters and an estimated weight of 13 tonnes.
The vertebrae have dorsoventrally elongate oval outlines, a characteristic feature shared only with Camarasaurus.
The genus is distinguished by the absence of cranial centrodiapophyseal laminae in its dorsal vertebrae.
It also features elongate intrapostzygapophyseal laminae, dorsal transverse processes reaching the height of neural spines, and an expanded distal end of the scapular blade.
The animal possessed a long neck with 14 vertebrae and a whip-like tail.
Its front legs were longer than its hind legs, giving its back a downward curve.
A potential specimen nicknamed "Big Monty" discovered in Montana has been claimed to measure an incredible 33 meters in length.
The genus Haplocanthosaurus was originally named by John Bell Hatcher in 1903.
The original name Haplocanthus was rejected because it was preoccupied by a fish genus.
Two incomplete skeletons were discovered in Colorado and described in 1903 as Haplocanthus priscus.
A second species, Haplocanthosaurus delfsi, was described by McIntosh and Williams in 1988.
This species was discovered by a college student named Edwin Delfs in Colorado and formally described in 1988.
Four specimens of Haplocanthosaurus are currently known: one of H. delfsi and three of H. priscus.
The type specimen of H. delfsi is the only known specimen complete enough to be mounted for display.
The mounted specimen is now located in the Cleveland Museum of Natural History.
There are 11 recorded fossil occurrences of Haplocanthosaurus.
Haplocanthosaurus was one of the smallest sauropods of the Morrison Formation.
Haplocanthosaurus belongs to the class Saurischia.
The parent group of Haplocanthosaurus is Diplodocoidea.
The genus is considered the last of the cetiosaurids.
José Bonaparte established the family Haplocanthosauridae in 1999 to classify Haplocanthosaurus separately from other sauropods.
Haplocanthosaurus lived in North America between 155 and 152 million years ago during the Late Jurassic.
Haplocanthosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 156 to 144 million years ago.
The time range for Haplocanthosaurus is from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian, between 154.8 and 143.1 million years ago.
Haplocanthosaurus lived in what is now North America.
The exact phylogenetic relationships of Haplocanthosaurus remain uncertain among scientists.
Studies have produced conflicting results, placing Haplocanthosaurus as a primitive macronarian, a very primitive diplodocoid related to Diplodocus, or a non-neosauropod eusauropod.
There is much controversy surrounding the "Big Monty" specimen, and very little is known about it.
